title: Sarga Twelve — verses 1–134
html:
Title of the sarga: none — the colophon of the edition gives no title for this sarga. Metre: upajāti (a mixture of indravajrā ——⏑——⏑⏑—⏑—— and upendravajrā ⏑—⏑——⏑⏑—⏑——; 11 syllables per pada); verse 87 — śālinī; verses 133–134 — mālinī. Total verses: 134 (verses 49 and 112 have six padas; 112 opens with a quotation of Bhagavatam 10.81.16 in the anuṣṭubh metre; 87 — śālinī; 120 — the chant "Rāma Rāghava…"; 133–134 — mālinī).

Contents of the passage: the Lord in Puri with Sarvabhauma; the departure for the south as far as the Godavari. - 1–9 — the Lord in Puri with Sarvabhauma; the darshan of Jagannatha. - 10–35 — Sarvabhauma's plan to instruct the Lord in Vedanta; the disputation; the Lord refutes the doctrine of non-duality; the four-armed form; hymns of praise. - 36–58 — the manuscript in Gopinatha's hand with Sarvabhauma's verse containing the word "Krishna"; the Lord, in ecstasy, returns to Puri; Gopinatha on the mercy shown to Sarvabhauma. - 59–77 — the mahaprasada: Sarvabhauma eats it without first washing; both are in ecstasy; Sarvabhauma is humbled. - 78–93 — eighteen interpretations of two stanzas from the Eleventh Canto; the verses vairāgya-vidyā… and kālān naṣṭaṁ… (the Lord tears up the leaf; Mukunda had copied them onto the wall); "bhakti-pade" instead of "mukti-pade". - 94–106 — eighteen days in Puri; the departure for the south; Sarvabhauma advises the Lord to meet Ramananda; Kurma-kshetra, the brahmana Kurma. - 107–117 — the leper Vasudeva is healed by an embrace; Kurma's lament. - 118–121 — Nrisimha-kshetra; the Lord's gait; the chant "Rāma Rāghava… Kṛṣṇa Keśava…". - 122–129 — the forests by the Godavari: peacocks, deer, parrots, cicadas, fearsome thickets and torrents. - 130–132 — hesitation: whether to speak with Ramananda; the Lord passes by and goes on south in ecstasy. - 133–134 (mālinī) — the wonder of the southerners: "A golden elephant? Meru set in motion? Lightning that does not fade?"

Verse 1

प्रविश्य सत्क्षेत्रमदभ्रलीलः
श्रीसार्वभौमालयमाययौ सः ।
आकस्मिकं वीक्ष्य जगन्मनोज्ञं
सन्न्यासिनं सोऽथ ननन्द विप्रः ॥१॥

praviśya sat-kṣetram adabhra-līlaḥ
śrī-sārvabhaumālayam āyayau saḥ |
ākasmikaṁ vīkṣya jagan-manojñaṁ [jñāna-manojñaṁ]
sannyāsinaṁ so 'tha nananda vipraḥ ||1||

praviśya — having entered; sat — the holy; kṣetram — Kshetra; adabhra — abundant; līlaḥ — [He whose] pastimes [are]; śrī-sārvabhauma — of Sri Sarvabhauma; ālayam — to the house; āyayau — came; saḥ — He; ākasmikam — unexpected; vīkṣya — having seen; jagat — to the world; manojñam — charming; sannyāsinam — the sannyasi; saḥ — that; atha — then; nananda — rejoiced; vipraḥ — brahmana.

1Having entered the holy Kshetra, He whose pastimes are boundless came to the house of Sri Sarvabhauma. And that brahmana, seeing the unexpected sannyasi who charms the world, rejoiced.

Note. The edition has ज्ञानमनोज्ञं ("charming by knowledge"), but the metre requires ⏑⏑ at the sixth and seventh syllables; we read jagan-manojñam. The Kshetra is Purushottama-kshetra (Puri). Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya was a celebrated Vedantist and logician at the court of Puri.

Verse 2

उत्थाय पाद्यादि समर्प्य भक्त्या
पुरो निवेद्यासनमप्युदारम् ।
कृतप्रणामो नु सुधीरमङ्ग
पप्रच्छ सर्वं विनयेन विप्रः ॥२॥

utthāya pādyādi samarpya bhaktyā
puro nivedyāsanam apy udāram |
kṛta-praṇāmo nu sudhīram aṅga
papraccha sarvaṁ vinayena vipraḥ ||2||

utthāya — having risen; pādya — water for [washing] the feet; ādi — and the rest; samarpya — having offered; bhaktyā — with devotion; puraḥ — before [Him]; nivedya — having presented; āsanam — a seat; api — also; udāram — excellent; kṛta — having made; praṇāmaḥ — obeisance; nu — indeed; su-dhīram — very composedly; aṅga — (a particle); papraccha — asked; sarvam — about everything; vinayena — with humility; vipraḥ — the brahmana.

2Rising, the brahmana with devotion offered water for [washing] the feet and the rest, set an excellent seat before [Him] as well, and, having made obeisance, very composedly and humbly asked about everything.

Verse 3

कुतः समेतोऽसि कुतो नु यासि
हृद्यो भवान्निर्भरशान्तदान्तः ।
इत्थं प्रभौ तेन यथार्थपृष्टे
तदेकनाथाः सकलं तदूचुः ॥३॥

kutaḥ sameto 'si kuto nu yāsi
hṛdyo bhavān nirbhara-śānta-dāntaḥ |
itthaṁ prabhau tena yathārtha-pṛṣṭe
tad-eka-nāthāḥ sakalaṁ tad ūcuḥ ||3||

kutaḥ — from where; sametaḥ asi — have You come; kutaḥ nu — where then; yāsi — are You going; hṛdyaḥ — charming; bhavān — You [are]; nirbhara — wholly; śānta — peaceful; dāntaḥ — [and] self-controlled; ittham — thus; prabhau — when the Lord; tena — by him; yathārtha — in substance; pṛṣṭe — had been asked; tat — Him; eka — as their only; nāthāḥ — [those who had as] Master; sakalam — all; tat — that; ūcuḥ — related.

3"From where have You come, and where are You going? You are charming, wholly peaceful and self-controlled." When the Lord had been asked thus by him in earnest, those whose only Master He was related all of it.

Verse 4

यथा-तथा तत् सकलं विदित्वा
ज्ञातं तदाज्ञातमिति प्रहृष्टः ।
ननन्द वृन्दारकवृन्दवन्द्य-
पादारविन्दस्य पुरः स विप्रः ॥४॥

yathā-tathā tat sakalaṁ viditvā
jñātaṁ tadā 'jñātam iti prahṛṣṭaḥ |
nananda vṛndāraka-vṛnda-vandya-
pādāravindasya puraḥ sa vipraḥ ||4||

yathā-tathā — just as it was; tat — that; sakalam — all; viditvā — having learned; jñātam — [is] known; tadā — now; ajñātam — the unknown; iti — thus [thinking]; prahṛṣṭaḥ — delighted; nananda — rejoiced; vṛndāraka — of the gods; vṛnda — by the host; vandya — worshipped; pāda — feet; aravindasya — of [Him whose] lotus; puraḥ — before; saḥ — that; vipraḥ — brahmana.

4Having learned all that just as it was, and delighted [at the thought] "Now the unknown has become known", that brahmana rejoiced before Him whose lotus feet are worshipped by the host of the gods.

Note. The edition has तदाज्ञातम्; we read tadā 'jñātam, "now the unknown [has become] known" (the metre is not affected).

Verse 5

ज्ञात्वाथ तस्याशयमेव सद्यः
स्वयं स्वपुत्रेण सदादरेण ।
प्रस्थापयामास सितेतराद्रौ
प्रभुं जगन्नाथदिदृक्षुमञ्जः ॥५॥

jñātvātha tasyāśayam eva sadyaḥ
svayaṁ sva-putreṇa sadādareṇa |
prasthāpayāmāsa sitetarādrau
prabhuṁ jagannātha-didṛkṣum añjaḥ ||5||

jñātvā — having understood; atha — then; tasya — His; āśayam — intention; eva — indeed; sadyaḥ — at once; svayam — himself; sva — with his own; putreṇa — son; sat — with due; ādareṇa — respect; prasthāpayāmāsa — sent; sita-itara — other than white (blue); adrau — to the mountain; prabhum — the Lord; jagannātha — Jagannatha; didṛkṣum — wishing to see; añjaḥ — straight.

5Then, having understood His intention, he at once, with due respect, himself sent the Lord, who wished to see Jagannatha, straight to the Blue Mountain together with his own son.

Note. Sitetarādri ("the mountain other than white") is Nilachala, the "Blue Mountain", the hill of Jagannatha's temple.

Verse 6

स तेन सार्धं समुपेत्य तत्र
सुखं ततः स्वैरमपि प्रविश्य ।
ददर्श नीलाचलमौलिरत्नं
तदातिसौख्याम्बुधिमग्न आसीत् ॥६॥

sa tena sārdhaṁ samupetya tatra
sukhaṁ tataḥ svairam api praviśya |
dadarśa nīlācala-mauli-ratnaṁ
tadāti-saukhyāmbudhi-magna āsīt ||6||

saḥ — He; tena — with him; sārdham — together; samupetya — having come; tatra — there; sukham — joyfully; tataḥ — then; svairam — freely; api — and; praviśya — having entered; dadarśa — beheld; nīlācala — of Nilachala; mauli — of the crown; ratnam — the jewel; tadā — then; ati — of the greatest; saukhya — bliss; ambudhi — in an ocean; magnaḥ — immersed; āsīt — was.

6Having come there together with him, and then joyfully and freely entering, He beheld the crest-jewel of Nilachala, and was then immersed in an ocean of the greatest bliss.

Verse 7

विलोक्य भूयो नतिभिः स्तवैश्च
नेत्राम्बुभिः स्वामभिषिच्य मूर्तिम् ।
प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य च पञ्चकृत्वः
कृच्छ्रेण तस्माद्बहिराययौ सः ॥७॥

vilokya bhūyo natibhiḥ stavaiś ca
netrāmbubhiḥ svām abhiṣicya mūrtim |
pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ca pañca-kṛtvaḥ
kṛcchreṇa tasmād bahir āyayau saḥ ||7||

vilokya — beholding; bhūyaḥ — again and again; natibhiḥ — with obeisances; stavaiḥ — with hymns; ca — and; netra — of the eyes; ambubhiḥ — with the waters; svām — His own; abhiṣicya — having bathed; mūrtim — form; pradakṣiṇīkṛtya — having circumambulated; ca — and; pañca-kṛtvaḥ — five times; kṛcchreṇa — with difficulty; tasmāt — from there; bahiḥ — out; āyayau — came; saḥ — He.

7Beholding [Him] again and again with obeisances and hymns, having bathed His own form with the waters of His eyes, and having circumambulated five times, He came out from there with difficulty.

Note. Svām mūrtim, "His own form", may mean His own body, drenched with tears, or Jagannatha, the Lord's own Deity form (?).

Verse 8

इति प्रभुस्तत्र विलोक्य कान्तं
ननन्द नीलाचलमौलिरत्नम् ।
स्वनामरत्नेन विधाय हारं
कण्ठे वहन्नेव रराज नित्यम् ॥८॥

iti prabhus tatra vilokya kāntaṁ
nananda nīlācala-mauli-ratnam |
sva-nāma-ratnena vidhāya hāraṁ
kaṇṭhe vahann eva rarāja nityam ||8||

iti — thus; prabhuḥ — the Lord; tatra — there; vilokya — beholding; kāntam — lovely; nananda — rejoiced; nīlācala — of Nilachala; mauli — of the crown; ratnam — the jewel; sva — of His own; nāma — name; ratnena — from the jewel; vidhāya — having made; hāram — a necklace; kaṇṭhe — on the neck; vahan — wearing; eva — indeed; rarāja — shone; nityam — always.

8Thus the Lord rejoiced, beholding there the lovely crest-jewel of Nilachala. Having made a necklace of the jewel of His own name, and ever wearing it on His neck, He shone.

Note. That is, He chanted the Name unceasingly.

Verse 9

मुकुन्ददत्तादिभिरात्मलोकैः
स तत्र नाथः कतिचिद्दिनानि ।
विलोकयन्नीलगिरीन्द्ररत्नं
निनाय कौतूहलपूर्णचित्तः ॥९॥

mukunda-dattādibhir ātma-lokaiḥ
sa tatra nāthaḥ katicid dināni |
vilokayan nīla-girīndra-ratnaṁ
nināya kautūhala-pūrṇa-cittaḥ ||9||

mukunda-datta — with Mukunda Datta; ādibhiḥ — and others; ātma — His own; lokaiḥ — with people; saḥ — He; tatra — there; nāthaḥ — the Lord; katicit — some; dināni — days; vilokayan — beholding; nīla — of the Blue; giri-indra — king of mountains; ratnam — the jewel; nināya — spent; kautūhala — with eagerness; pūrṇa — filled; cittaḥ — [with] heart.

9With Mukunda Datta and others of His own, the Lord spent some days there beholding the jewel of the Blue King of mountains, His heart filled with eagerness.

Verse 10

स एकदा चेतसि सार्वभौमो
महीसुराग्र्यः कलयांचकार ।
प्रभावमैश्वर्यमिदं समस्तं
मनुष्यभावादविदन् कृपालोः ॥१०॥

sa ekadā cetasi sārvabhaumo
mahīsurāgryaḥ kalayāṁ cakāra |
prabhāvam aiśvaryam idaṁ samastaṁ
manuṣya-bhāvād avidan kṛpāloḥ ||10||

saḥ — that; ekadā — once; cetasi — in the mind; sārvabhaumaḥ — Sarvabhauma; mahī-sura — of the gods of the earth (brahmanas); agryaḥ — the foremost; kalayāṁ cakāra — considered; prabhāvam — the power; aiśvaryam — the majesty; idam — this; samastam — all; manuṣya — human; bhāvāt — because of the condition; avidan — not knowing; kṛpāloḥ — of the Merciful One.

10Once Sarvabhauma, the foremost of the brahmanas, reflected in his mind, not knowing, because of [His] human condition, all this power and majesty of the Merciful One.

Note. Verses 10–16 are Sarvabhauma's reflections.

Verse 11

अखण्डपाण्डित्यसमुद्रवीचि-
प्रवाहकल्लोलकुलैरमन्दै-
र्यस्य प्रकामं बधिरीकृतोऽभू-
द्बृहस्पतिर्जाड्यमयं समेतः ॥११॥

akhaṇḍa-pāṇḍitya-samudra-vīci-
pravāha-kallola-kulair amandair
yasya prakāmaṁ badhirīkṛto 'bhūd
bṛhaspatir jāḍyamayaṁ sametaḥ ||11||

akhaṇḍa — of unbroken; pāṇḍitya — learning; samudra — of the ocean; vīci — of the waves; pravāha — of the streams; kallola — of the billows; kulaiḥ — by the masses; amandaiḥ — mighty; yasya — by whose; prakāmam — utterly; badhirīkṛtaḥ — deafened; abhūt — became; bṛhaspatiḥ — Brihaspati; jāḍya — stupor; mayam — consisting of; sametaḥ — having fallen into.

11He by whose mighty masses of billows, by whose streams of waves from the ocean of unbroken learning, Brihaspati himself was utterly deafened and fell into a stupor —

Note. Yasya ("he by whose") is taken up by sa eva ("that very one") in verse 12, which points to Sarvabhauma (?). Brihaspati is the preceptor of the gods, the very model of learning. The Gosvami edition (GGM) has the same text.

Verse 12

स एव सम्भावितदम्भराशि-
र्गभीरधीर्यत्प्रभुपादपद्मम् ।
न वेद तन्नो खलु चित्रमेत-
न्न वेत्ति पाण्डित्यकुलादिलेशम् ॥१२॥

sa eva sambhāvita-dambha-rāśir
gabhīra-dhīr yat prabhu-pāda-padmam |
na veda tan no khalu citram etan
na vetti pāṇḍitya-kulādi-leśam ||12||

saḥ eva — that very one; sambhāvita — esteemed; dambha — of pride; rāśiḥ — a heap; gabhīra — deep; dhīḥ — [of] intellect; yat — that; prabhu — of the Lord; pāda — of the feet; padmam — the lotus; na veda — did not know; tat — that; no khalu — not at all; citram — a wonder; etat — this; na vetti — does not know; pāṇḍitya — of the learning; kula — of the lineage; ādi — and so on; leśam — a particle.

12— he, that very one, a heap of esteemed pride, deep of intellect, did not know the lotus feet of the Lord. That is no wonder at all: he does not know even a particle of His learning, lineage and so on.

Note. The edition has yan na … na veda, a double negative; the Gosvami edition (GGM) reads yat prabhu-pāda-padmaṁ na veda, and so we read: "that he did not know the feet of the Lord is no wonder".

Verse 13

असौ महात्मा पुरुषप्रधानो
वयस्थ एव न्यसनं चकार ।
यदीदृशं स्वान्तरलं तदालं
विचिन्तितैर्नस्त्वयि कष्टमेतत् ॥१३॥

asau mahātmā puruṣa-pradhāno
vayastha eva nyasanaṁ cakāra |
yadīdṛśaṁ svāntaralaṁ tad ālaṁ (?)
vicintitair nas tvayi kaṣṭam etat ||13||

asau — this; mahātmā — great soul; puruṣa — among men; pradhānaḥ — the foremost; vayasthaḥ — while young; eva — indeed; nyasanam — renunciation; cakāra — has made; yadi — if; īdṛśam — such; sva-antaram — His heart; alam — enough; tat — then; ālam (?) — enough; vicintitaiḥ — with deliberations; naḥ — our; tvayi — for You; kaṣṭam — hard; etat — this.

13"This great soul, the foremost among men, has embraced renunciation while still young. If such is His heart, then enough of our deliberations. But for You this is hard!

Note. The second half is obscure. The edition has स्वान्तरलं तदालं, perhaps corrupt (?). The Gosvami edition (GGM) reads yad īdṛśaṁ svāntar alaṁ tadā laṁ / vicintitair na tvayi kaṣṭam etat, with na: "this is not hard for You".

Verse 14

अनेकधा पुरुषरत्नचिह्नै-
र्मनोरमः सर्वजगज्जनस्य ।
कथं नु कालं गमयिष्यतीमं
सन्न्यासधर्मप्रतिपालनेन ॥१४॥

anekadhā puruṣa-ratna-cihnair
manoramaḥ sarva-jagaj-janasya |
kathaṁ nu kālaṁ gamayiṣyatīmaṁ
sannyāsa-dharma-pratipālanena ||14||

anekadhā — manifold; puruṣa — among men; ratna — of a jewel; cihnaiḥ — by the marks; manoramaḥ — charming; sarva — of the whole; jagat — world; janasya — to the people; katham nu — how indeed; kālam — time; gamayiṣyati — will He pass; imam — this; sannyāsa — of sannyasa; dharma — of the duties; pratipālanena — by the observance.

14He who by the manifold marks of a jewel among men charms the people of the whole world — how indeed will He pass this time in observing the duties of sannyasa?

Note. In the first pada the fifth syllable (pu- of puruṣa) is light, where both indravajrā and upendravajrā require a heavy one; perhaps the poetic form pūruṣa was intended (?).

Verse 15

असौ महावंशसमुद्भवश्च
महाशयश्चाल्पवयोविकाशः ।
कलौ तदर्हां यतितां सुदुर्गां
कथं तरिष्यत्यहहातिकष्टम् ॥१५॥

asau mahā-vaṁśa-samudbhavaś ca
mahāśayaś cālpa-vayo-vikāśaḥ |
kalau tad-arhāṁ yatitāṁ sudurgāṁ
kathaṁ tariṣyaty ahahāti-kaṣṭam ||15||

asau — He; mahā — of a great; vaṁśa — family; samudbhavaḥ — born; ca — and; mahā-āśayaḥ — magnanimous; ca — and; alpa — scarcely; vayaḥ — of age; vikāśaḥ — [whose] blossoming; kalau — in Kali; tat — for it; arhām — befitting; yatitām — asceticism; su-durgām — most arduous; katham — how; tariṣyati — will He get through; ahaha — alas; ati — exceedingly; kaṣṭam — hard.

15He is born of a great family, He is magnanimous, and His youth has scarcely blossomed. How will He get through, in [the age of] Kali, the most arduous asceticism befitting it? Alas, how exceedingly hard!

Verse 16

तदेतमत्यन्तसुशान्तचित्तं
संश्राव्य वेदान्तमजस्रमेव ।
करोमि वैराग्यरसेन भास्व-
ज्ज्ञानैकतानेन च मोक्षपान्थम् ॥१६॥

tad etam atyanta-suśānta-cittaṁ
saṁśrāvya vedāntam ajasram eva |
karomi vairāgya-rasena bhāsvaj-
jñānaika-tānena ca mokṣa-pāntham ||16||

tat — therefore; etam — Him; atyanta — wholly; su-śānta — very peaceful; cittam — [whose] heart; saṁśrāvya — having made to hear; vedāntam — the Vedanta; ajasram — unceasingly; eva — indeed; karomi — I shall make; vairāgya — of detachment; rasena — by the taste; bhāsvat — to radiant; jñāna — knowledge; eka-tānena — [and] by whole-hearted devotion; ca — and; mokṣa — to liberation; pāntham — a wayfarer.

16Therefore, by making Him, whose heart is wholly at peace, hear the Vedanta unceasingly, I shall make Him a wayfarer on the road to liberation, through the taste of detachment and through whole-hearted devotion to radiant knowledge."

Note. Sarvabhauma means to instruct the Lord in Advaita Vedanta. Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita, Madhya 6: for seven days Sarvabhauma expounds the Brahma-sutras.

Verse 17

इत्यस्य हृन्मन्त्रितमाकलय्य
प्रभुः प्रफुल्लाम्बुजमञ्जुलास्यः ।
व्याप्य त्रिलोकीं स्फुरितानुकम्पा-
